# CYBR LIGHT live demo

The default view is the real current RGB WebGPU path tracer. Use the scene selector for three procedural transport proofs, four native-authored browser studies, the original GEO exports, and the cleared six-module instrument including cached FLIP frames. The model gallery is the 39-model cleared subset; no substitute geometry is used.

The Forest raster link opens the actual procedural stand: original geometry, 1,220,375 original instance placements, cached sun shadows and approximate sky lighting. It is rasterization, not spectral/path-tracing parity. The forest path-traced reference remains available through the original controls and depends on sufficient browser/GPU limits.

All restored runtime assets are byte-checked against the preserved current capture. Large gzip streams are delivered as static parts and concatenated before the original decoder sees them. No mesh, instance, material, fluid frame or shader math is downsampled or rewritten. The live build adds only the large-file delivery adapter and filters unavailable scene choices. Original renderer source and implementation digests are retained separately.

Original forest authoring state and exporter are outside standalone LIGHT. Exact runtime restoration is verified; regeneration from authoring source is a different workflow. Cached FLIP is recorded geometry, not live fluid simulation.

The composite instrument's four files match the cleared public portfolio package exactly. Current MakeHuman/Quaternius mannequin provenance and motion credits are retained under LICENSES. Source/code GPLv2, original native MIT and meshoptimizer MIT notices remain separate.

Not shipped: Observatory interior/full scene and Drowned Geode exports, their gallery derivatives, and the original pile/million-model bakes that depend on those inputs. Their imported-room/scanned-input attribution is unresolved in the inspected records. Large differential/geode authoring caches and old private Git history are not part of this site. Five geode texture conversions have known source names but no verified license/source records here.

Existing moving optical noise, forest lighting/LOD approximation and clearing-camera branch intersection remain. No new GPU run was made for this publication while another task owns the slot; prior matched hardware validation and current CPU asset/source checks are recorded in the source validation notes. No universal FPS guarantee is made.

The downloadable source ZIP contains the complete curated native C++/Python, optional CUDA/OptiX and browser source from cleanup commit 33d2a2cc6df362dfcf902082f68e58051145579f, without private Git history or companion caches. Native offline build/run commands are in its root README. The live client modules, delivery adapter and asset parts are served directly by this site.
